授業概要
「公・私」は人間の活動とその環境を考える基本的な概念である。しかし、「公」と「私」は対概念でありながら、その境界はどこにあるのか？もしくは境界はあるのか？近現代社会においては、公的権力による私的領域への介入が顕在化し、一見私的な問題は実は社会構造と関連する。一方で、公的領域が私有化され、市民が私的領域に閉じ込む傾向も見られる。また、インターネットの発達とソーシャルメディアの普及により、公と私の区別は曖昧化される。どこまでが私的領域か？どこまでが公的領域か？何が私的問題か？何が公的問題か？「公」と「私」は人間環境においてどう区別、または関係する（すべき）か？基本的な概念であるからこそ社会、教育、空間、心理などのあらゆる側面から再認識、再検討する価値がある。
令和 8 年度のシリーズ「人間環境学」では、「公・私」をテーマとし、人間環境学を構成する多様な分野の教員がその専門分野の視点から公・私について論じる。本授業を通じ、人間環境学に関わる多様な視点やアプローチを学び、異分野との相互理解や協働基盤を築くとともに、自発的かつ批判的な思考力を養うことを期待する。
The concepts of the “public” and the “private” constitute a fundamental framework for understanding human activity and its environment. Yet, although “public” and “private” are often treated as oppositional categories, where exactly does the boundary between them lie? Or does such a boundary exist at all?
In modern and contemporary societies, the intrusion of public authority into the private sphere has become increasingly visible, revealing that issues appearing to be private are in fact closely connected to broader social structures. At the same time, the privatisation of the public sphere and the tendency for citizens to retreat into private life are also evident. Furthermore, with the development of the internet and the widespread use of social media, the distinction between public and private has become increasingly blurred.
To what extent does the private sphere exist? Where does the public sphere begin? What constitutes a private issue, and what qualifies as a public one? How should “public” and “private” be distinguished or related within the context of the human environment? Precisely because these are fundamental concepts, they deserve renewed examination from multiple perspectives, such as social, educational, spatial, and psychological.
In the 2026 academic year, the Human-Environment Studies series will focus on the theme ‘Public and Private”. Faculty members from various disciplines will explore this theme from their respective expertise. Through this course, students are expected to gain a variety of perspectives and approaches within human environmental studies, to establish a foundation for interdisciplinary understanding and collaboration, and to develop independent and critical thinking skills.
